name: Free France
alt: Provisional Government of the French Republic

predecessors.name: French Africa
predecessors.text: Chad, Cameroon, the Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari, the first colonies to rally in August 1940

successors.name: French Fourth Republic
successors.text: France, liberated in 1944, and the empire under the Provisional Government of the French Republic created on 3 June 1944

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the equatorial lands and Djibouti, which Cliopatria returns to its French Africa row in 1943

ledger.x: Summer 1940: French India and the South Pacific colonies join.
18 June 1940: de Gaulle's appeal at the BBC founds Free France.
26 August 1940: Chad rallies.
27 August 1940: Cameroon rallies.
29 August 1940: the Middle Congo rallies.
30 August 1940: Ubangi-Shari rallies.
27 October 1940: the Free French attack Vichy Gabon.
12 November 1940: Gabon falls to Free France, completing the equatorial colonies.
12 November 1940: the Battle of Gabon ends.
8 June 1941: the Syria-Lebanon campaign begins.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 14 July 1941: the Vichy forces give in.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: July 1941: Syria and Lebanon pass under Free France.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 24 December 1941: Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.
13 July 1942: Free France becomes Fighting France.
28 December 1942: French Somaliland leaves Vichy.
First months of 1943: the French Americas join.
1943: the equatorial lands and Djibouti go back to French Africa.
3 June 1943: the French Committee of National Liberation.
June 1944: the Free French hold on Syria and Lebanon passes to the Provisional Government.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 3 June 1944: the Provisional Government of the French Republic takes over.

wars.name: Battle of Gabon
wars.outcome: Free French victory: Gabon, the last of the equatorial colonies, is occupied between 27 October and 12 November 1940.

wars.name: Battle of Dakar
wars.outcome: Failure: 'On 23 September 1940, the Royal Navy and Free French forces under Gaulle launched Operation Menace'; 'British and Free French forces withdrew on 25 September'.

wars.name: Syria-Lebanon campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: ceasefire 12 July and the Convention of Acre on 14 July 1941; 'Syria and Lebanon taken over by Free France'.

wars.name: Battle of Madagascar
wars.outcome: British and Commonwealth conquest of Vichy Madagascar in Operation Ironclad ('From 5 May to 6 November 1942').

certainty.note: The equatorial colonies' frontiers were administrative lines, approximate on the map; the Syrian and Lebanese frontiers are those of the mandate.
